newsitem.title: USA: IBM shutting down InfoSage service.
newsitem.headline: IBM shutting down InfoSage service.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp is shutting down its InfoSage Internet news service because it competes with IBM customers, IBM Chairman and Chief Executive Louis Gerstner said Wedneswday.
"Our customers didn't like the idea that InfoSage pushed their brands into the background," Gerstner said in the keynote speech at the Internet World trade show here.
IBM does not wish to compete with its customers, he said.
InfoSage is an Internet-based service that gathers stories at the request of a subscriber and provides a personalized news service tailored to a customer's request.

News is delivered either to a customer's electronic mail address or to a company or individual World Wide Web site. Some stories are snippets and do not always identify the source of the news, so the brand on the news was lost.
Content providers on the InfoSage service include Reuters Holdings Plc's New Media; IAC (Information Access Co), a Thomson Corp company, and Standard and Poor's Corp.
As of November 27, InfoSage stopped taking subscriptions.
